expertise: Source contract authority and conditional-rule review

semantic_votes.rationale: The rule is professionally correct and actionable: before introducing an extension abstraction it requires named consumers, distinct change reasons, ownership, and likely evolution, and it prescribes direct code or configuration when variation remains unproven or locally owned. Its placement under extensibility-design High-Value Rules and the Registry Trigger bounds it to an actual task-local extension decision. It does not impose trust or rollback mechanisms universally: adjacent source rules condition origin, authenticity, or integrity controls on executables crossing install or update trust boundaries, authenticated metadata on existing update channels, and rehearsed last-known-good rollback on mutable or consequential activation; config-only and static extensions instead require evidence-backed non-applicability.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies when extensibility-design evaluates a proposed extension point, plugin, policy hook, configuration variation, or other shared variation boundary. It does not apply when no task-local extensibility decision exists. Executable trust controls apply only when artifacts cross install or update trust boundaries; update-metadata authentication applies to an existing update channel; rollback proof applies when activation is mutable or consequential. Config-only or static extensions may establish inspected, evidence-backed non-applicability.
semantic_votes.decision_owner: The assigned extensibility-design analysis-agent or review-agent owns the variation-evidence decision; the relevant host, policy, or threat-model authority owns disputed executable trust, update-channel, activation, and rollback conditions.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Keep the variation in direct code or configuration until current consumers, independent change reasons, ownership, and likely evolution support a stable extension boundary. Record inspected evidence for any inapplicable trust, update, or rollback control, and escalate unclear ownership, trust or tenant crossings, corrupting failure, unavailable isolation, or unproved last-known-good recovery.

semantic_votes.rationale: This is a valid contextual evidence gate, not an unconditional implementation mechanism. Its placement in Stop Conditions governs a claim that a particular control is inapplicable and makes that claim actionable by requiring a concise rationale tied to inspected evidence. The surrounding source supplies the non-applicability boundaries: executable origin, authenticity, or integrity applies only across install or update trust boundaries; authenticated metadata applies to existing update channels; last-known-good rollback applies to mutable or consequential activation; config-only or static extensions may document why those controls do not apply. Requiring evidence prevents silent omission without making every control mandatory.
semantic_votes.authority_or_condition: Applies only when an assigned reviewer or analyst concludes that a control named by extensibility-design is inapplicable to the current extension boundary. It does not apply when the Skill itself is out of scope because no extensibility decision exists. A non-applicability claim must identify the control, its trigger, and inspected facts showing the trigger is absent; where trust, update, tenant, consequence, or rollback conditions are unclear, the source requires escalation rather than waiver.
semantic_votes.decision_owner: The assigned extensibility-design analysis-agent or review-agent owns the documented applicability assessment; the relevant host, policy, threat-model, or operational owner confirms disputed trust, update, consequence, and rollback facts.
semantic_votes.mitigation: Record the evaluated control, trigger condition, inspected evidence that the trigger is absent, residual risk, and residual owner. Do not claim non-applicability when an executable crosses a trust boundary, an existing update channel lacks authenticated metadata, or mutable or consequential activation lacks rehearsed last-known-good recovery; satisfy the control or escalate.
